head: f80d776d9b431a057bc53089bcf6cdc80ed2fc1f
summary:
HF-026 is fixed as specified, but the two fix obligations code review filed against build-slice (O-001, O-002) are still open, so the verdict is partial.

What works: tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1:176-183 now reads the whole line and removes the scratch copy when %TEMP% has a space, and when TEMP and TMP point at different folders. Checked with:
- the slice's own test in both modes (stand-in harness, and the real harness.py under the engine's python);
- my own probe, which runs RuleCases' own Invoke-HarnessRaw against the real harness.py;
- RuleCases -Case All against the real engine: 429 checks passed, 0 failed, 404 s, and no new fsa-* folder was left in this machine's real %TEMP%.

The .NET suite passed (400/0/0) and all 61 fitness rules hold.

What doesn't: running the same probe against the current tree, three TEMP shapes still leave the harness's full repo copy behind:
- **O-001, 8.3 short-form TEMP:** the harness printed `...\FS5E7B~1\LONGNA~1\...\fsa-rules-y4eyzu12` and the folder was left behind (left=1).
- **O-002, non-ASCII TEMP:** the harness printed `Jos\xe9 Smith` and the real `José Smith\Temp\fsa-rules-qtbpp8ap` was left behind (left=1).
- **TMPDIR set:** the scratch went to TMPDIR and was left behind (left=1). The build declared this gap as left open.

These are the same leak HF-026 is about, in other local-account shapes. The build has not discharged either obligation: build-slice has one attempt, made before code review filed them, and HEAD is still that commit (f80d776).

One unrelated failure: tests/bugs/SL-069-RuleCasesDeriveCounts.Tests.ps1 fails before it runs RuleCases.ps1 at all. The file is checked out with CRLF (core.autocrlf=true), so its here-strings already hold CRLF. `.Replace("`n", "`r`n")` then writes CR CR LF into the scratch copy of ArchitectureRulesTests.cs, and rules-parity refuses to read line 158. This comes from SL-069's test and this slice did not cause it.

There is no loop: one build attempt, one review.

checks.what: SL-069 derive-counts test, which copies RuleCases.ps1 into a scratch tree
checks.evidence: Exit 1 at the test's own setup (line 96), before RuleCases.ps1 runs: 'rules-parity: CANNOT-READ tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/ArchitectureRulesTests.cs:158: a line break ... (U+000D)'. Cause: core.autocrlf=true, and git ls-files --eol shows the test as i/lf w/crlf. Its here-strings therefore hold CRLF, and Add-Before's .Replace("`n","`r`n") writes CR CR LF. The worktree's ArchitectureRulesTests.cs itself is clean (CRLF=195, bare CR=0). This slice did not touch the test, rules-parity.ps1 or the .cs file, so it did not cause this failure.

checks.what: Survey of the real %TEMP% for scratch copies left behind
checks.evidence: 26 pre-existing fsa-rules-* folders, dated 2026-09-28 11:41 to 20:54 IST, all before this slice opened (21:11 IST). 8 of them are fsa-rules-case-* (RuleCases' own New-TempDir), each paired with a harness scratch 1-2 s later. That pattern fits interrupted runs, not HF-026, because TEMP=TMP here and the path has no space. Not attributed and not deleted. Recorded as an observation, not a defect of this slice.

criteria.criterion: HF-026: RuleCases' Invoke-HarnessRaw reads the harness's 'scratch kept at' path as the rest of the line, so a %TEMP% with a space is not cut at the space and the scratch copy is removed
criteria.how: RuleCases.ps1:176 uses '(?m)^harness: scratch kept at (.+?)\s*$'. Checked with the SL-076 Space shape (stand-in), the -Shape Python run (real harness.py, spaced TEMP; the folder was removed and none was left), and my own probe with the real harness.py and the AST-extracted function (spaced long TEMP, left=0).

criteria.criterion: HF-026: the folder is accepted when its leaf is fsa-rules-* and its parent is GetTempPath or $env:TEMP, so TEMP≠TMP no longer leaks
criteria.how: RuleCases.ps1:179-181. In the SL-076 TempNotTmp shape GetTempPath returned tmp-a and the TEMP (tmp-b) scratch was removed. The Python shape confirmed that the real harness.py writes to TEMP and the scratch was removed. The Refused shape showed that folders elsewhere, non-fsa-rules folders and nested fsa-rules folders are left alone.

criteria.criterion: No regression in the project's suites that touch the change
criteria.how: .NET suite 400/0/0. Fitness: 61/61 rules hold. RuleCases -Case All against the real engine: 429 ok, 0 FAIL, exit 0, no new scratch left in real %TEMP%. The SL-069 GuardRule and SettledCountProbe GuardRule checks pass. SL-069-RuleCasesDeriveCounts fails in its own setup on a CRLF here-string defect this slice did not touch.

obligations.evidence: Not discharged. HEAD is still f80d776, the only build attempt, and RuleCases.ps1:179 still compares the harness's raw parent with GetFullPath-expanded TMP/TEMP. Reproduced now with the real harness.py and the AST-extracted Invoke-HarnessRaw: TEMP=TMP='C:\Users\sshub\AppData\Local\Temp\FS5E7B~1\LONGNA~1\AppData\Local\Temp' exited 2, printed 'scratch kept at ...\LONGNA~1\...\fsa-rules-y4eyzu12', and the folder was left behind. The SL-076 test has no ShortName shape. Owed to build-slice.

Not discharged. The path is still taken whole from the line rather than by leaf. Reproduced now: TEMP=TMP='...\José Smith\Temp' printed 'scratch kept at ...\Jos\xe9 Smith\Temp\fsa-rules-qtbpp8ap', and the real folder was left behind. The SL-076 test has no NonAscii shape. Owed to build-slice.

not_reached: A real Windows account whose profile path has a space, where Windows itself sets TEMP/TMP. Every spaced, TEMP≠TMP, 8.3 and non-ASCII shape here was simulated by setting TEMP/TMP in a child process on the sshub account, whose TEMP is C:\Users\sshub\AppData\Local\Temp with TEMP=TMP.

Whether Windows 11 26200 actually sets TEMP in 8.3 form for a long or spaced account name. O-001's premise ('commonly') was reproduced only with a FileSystemObject ShortPath, not with a real account profile.
A real MSYS/Git Bash shell exporting TMPDIR. Only simulated by setting the env var; the build declared the gap as left open.

What left the 26 pre-existing fsa-rules-* folders in this machine's real %TEMP% (11:41-20:54 IST today, before this slice). The conditions here rule out HF-026, and the fsa-rules-case-* pairs suggest interrupted RuleCases runs, but this was not established.
RuleCases' Invoke-HarnessRaw under Windows PowerShell 5.1. RuleCases was run only under pwsh 7.
